deepdive.sec: Mining Consumables & Mineral-Processing Equipment (picks-and-shovels to global mining)

bull_bear.body:
- Major leverage event: ~$838m Molycop debt + INR1,500 cr parent acquisition debt (Std Chartered/Axis/EXIM) on top of INR1,700 cr already raised. Molycop debt already paid down ~$220m (from ~$1,050m to $838m) pre-close.
- Stated priority: deleverage to ~3x within 3-4 years via revenue + cost synergies + non-core asset sales.
- Working capital improved FY26 (better collections + payables); DSO target 100-105 days.
- Capex self-funded from internal accruals + existing facilities.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **Consumables execution credibility:** flat FY26 vs repeated 15% guidance (FY24 10%, FY25 11%) — analyst pushback; "timing/logistics" narrative must convert to H1 FY27 revenue (the swing item).
- **Logistics / Middle-East shipping:** vessel + container shortage stranded FG; finding alternate routes but a recurring geopolitical exposure.
- **Molycop integration & leverage:** ~$838m+ debt; only 1 month consol in Q1; ~$30m more one-time transaction cost hits Q1 FY27 P&L; FY-end alignment Jun→Mar adds reporting noise.
- **Molycop growth deferral:** Cobre Panama + Grasberg restarts pushed to FY28 → only ~3% FY27 growth; volume/market-share not disclosed (transparency gap).
- **Chile regulatory slippage:** commercial production approval-gated; revenue could push to FY28.
- **Commodity/steel pricing:** Molycop revenue is steel-conversion linked; RM volatility on Tega consumables.
- **Equipment lumpiness:** project execution swings (H1 +65 / H2 flat) — single-order dependent (NMDC).
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: - Detailed, multi-speaker (group + Molycop CFO/COO on call) — good transparency on the deal mechanics (debt, transaction costs, synergy framework, 100/200-day plans). However, somewhat defensive on the repeated consumables miss — declined to cut the 15% guidance despite three soft years, leaning on "cyclicality" and a logistics one-off. Pushed back accurately on an analyst conflating the $30m transaction cost with an operating "loss." Declined to share Molycop volume/market-share data. Overall credible but the consumables guidance now carries a show-me burden.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- This is a re-platforming quarter: post-Molycop, Tega goes from a ~INR1,770 cr Indian consumables/equipment maker to a >~$1.7bn global mining-solutions platform — but FY27 reported numbers will be messy (1-month Molycop consol, ~$30m one-time Q1 cost, FY-end migration, lower blended margin).
- The "flat consumables" is the real debate, not Molycop: order book +18% and ~INR100 cr of deferred revenue support the timing story, but it's the third consecutive year below the 15% line — H1 FY27 execution is the single most important verification item.
- Molycop is a steel-linked, capex-light, ~12%-margin cash cow bought largely with debt — the thesis is deleveraging + synergy capture, not organic growth (only ~3% FY27).
- Tega is a leveraged play on the copper/gold mining-capex supercycle: it sells the picks-and-shovels (liners, grinding media, beneficiation plants) into electrification-driven copper demand — a derivative "Grid-Capex / energy-transition" beneficiary one layer removed.
- Chile plant + Japanese-collaboration equipment product are FY27/FY28 optionality, both back-end loaded (Q3-Q4).
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Net cash from operating activities was Rs. 1,950.3 Mn, partially funding capex; the company maintained a net debt position with total borrowings of Rs. 2,619.3 Mn.
- No dividend or share buyback is mentioned; retained earnings increased equity to Rs. 13,966.9 Mn, suggesting reinvestment over shareholder payouts.

business.body:
- **Consumables (~84% of rev, FY26 flat):** mill liners / wear solutions / screens / spares & conversion; bespoke, design-led, 3-6 month order-to-revenue lag. FY26 weakness attributed to (a) orders bunching into Feb-Mar and (b) Middle-East shipping disruption (no vessel/container availability) stranding FG. Q4 consumables rev INR440.6 cr (vs INR456.8 cr, -INR16.2 cr). Normalised Q4 consumables EBITDA margin ~27.7% (adding back INR776 mn one-off).
- **Equipment / Tega McNally Minerals (~16%, +25% FY26):** dense-media/mineral-beneficiation plants & project equipment (NMDC-type). H1 +65.4% then H2 flat on project-execution timing (depends on customer site readiness). EBITDA margin 12-13%.
- **Molycop (acquired 01-Jun-26, with Apollo Funds minority):** global grinding-media (high-chrome + forged balls) for mining comminution; ~$1,539m FY26 (Jun-end) revenue, ~12% EBITDA, ~1% growth; capex-light (~2-3% of revenue). Mgmt declined to disclose volume split (high-chrome vs forged) or market share for now. Consolidates from 01-Jun (1 month in Q1 FY27); FY-end migrating Jun→Mar.

- **Q4 FY26 (this):** Consol rev INR1,774 cr (+5% YoY), adj EBITDA 22% (INR397 cr); Q4 rev INR563 cr, adj EBITDA 29%. Consumables FY26 FLAT (vs 15% guide) — blamed Feb-Mar order bunching + Middle-East shipping (~INR50 cr FG stranded); order book INR1,206 cr (+18% pending YoY), INR906 cr executable in 12m. Equipment +25% (H1 +65/H2 flat), margin 12-13%. **Molycop acquisition closed 01-Jun-2026** (with Apollo Funds minority; ~$1,539m rev, ~12% EBITDA, ~1% growth, Jun FY-end → migrating to Mar); +$838m Molycop debt + INR1,500 cr parent debt; ~$30m one-time transaction cost to hit Q1 FY27. Exceptionals INR839 mn (Molycop costs INR775 mn + labour code INR64 mn).
- _Next Q (Q1 FY27) → check: (1) does consumables H1 execution finally convert the +18% order book / ~INR100 cr deferred FG into revenue? (2) Molycop 1-month consol numbers + the ~$30m transaction-cost hit; (3) FY-end migration Jun→Mar reporting; (4) deleveraging progress vs 3x/3-4yr target + any non-core asset sale; (5) Chile commissioning Q3 + regulatory approvals; (6) Japanese-collaboration equipment product launch Q3; (7) Molycop growth still ~3% (Cobre Panama/Grasberg now FY28); (8) blended margin dilution once Molycop fully consolidates._

outlook.body:
- **Tega consumables:** reaffirmed long-term ~15%+ CAGR (despite FY24 10% / FY25 11% / FY26 flat — mgmt calls it cyclicality, declined to cut guidance).
- **Tega equipment:** ~25% growth in FY27 (matching FY26); EBITDA margin 12-13%.
- **Tega blended EBITDA margin:** ~21-22% (ex-Molycop synergies).
- **Molycop:** ~3% revenue growth FY27 (high-level; revised down from a ~6-8% earlier hope because Cobre Panama + Grasberg mine restarts now deferred to FY28, not FY27); FY26 (Jun-end) ~1% growth, ~12% EBITDA margin; FY26 revenue $1,539m.
- **Deleveraging:** bring Molycop debt to ~3x leverage within 3-4 years (3 levers: revenue synergies in Tega, cost synergies in Molycop, non-core asset sales).
- **Capex FY27:** Chile plant ~$25-30m (final tranche, completes FY27); Tega sustaining ~INR50-60 cr; Molycop maintenance ~$20m (growth capex TBD); ~$55m total — funded from internal accruals + already-placed borrowing, no fresh capex debt.
- **Chile plant:** civil ~50-60% done; commission early Q3 FY27; commercial production gated on regulatory approvals → revenue booking only from end-Q4 FY27 or FY28.
- **New equipment product:** aggregate-business launch via Japanese-company collaboration, in Q3 FY27.
- **Working capital:** maintain DSO ~100-105 days.
outlook.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)

outlook.body:
- Consolidated (Tega) order book INR1,206 cr at 31-Mar-26; INR906 cr executable in 12 months; pending order +18% YoY (heavy booking in Feb-Mar).
- Consumables: order intake grew strongly (executable pending +17%); revenue lag is the 3-6 month bespoke design-build cycle plus the March logistics slip — ~INR50 cr stranded finished goods ≈ ~INR100 cr deferred revenue into H1 FY27.
- Equipment: continues bidding project business (FY26 was lifted by an NMDC win); expects fresh project bookings in FY27 + the new Japanese-collaboration product; tailwinds from capex in power, mining and mineral beneficiation.
- Geographic expansion in equipment: success in Canada; participating in CIS (clarified "Russia" = CIS) and project work; growing Middle-East beneficiation export footprint.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body:
- **Molycop synergies (un-quantified):** revenue synergies booked in Tega (cross-sell consumables into Molycop's customer base), cost synergies in Molycop, plus non-core asset divestments — detailed 100/200-day plans underway; guidance to come once finalised. Explicitly NOT in the 15% Tega guidance.
- **Copper/gold supercycle pull-through:** mgmt framed structural demand — gold demand >5,000t (2025 record, supply +~1%/yr); copper demand +3%/yr vs supply +2%, +40% by 2040 needing ~$250bn and ~80 new mines → more mining capex = more consumables/grinding-media/equipment demand.
- **Chile plant:** new consumables capacity nearshoring to Latin-American copper belt (commission Q3 FY27).
- **New equipment product** (Japanese collaboration, aggregate business, Q3 FY27) — forward revenue optionality.
- **Geographic equipment expansion:** Canada, CIS, Middle-East beneficiation exports.

deepdive.thesis: Tega closed FY26 a transformational quarter behind: consolidated revenue INR1,774 cr (+5% YoY) with 22% adjusted EBITDA, but the headline is the 01-Jun-2026 completion of the Molycop grinding-media acquisition (with Apollo Funds), which roughly triples group scale (Molycop ~$1.54bn revenue) and adds ~$838m of debt — making FY27 a deleveraging-and-integration year. The core Tega consumables book disappointed (full-year flat vs 15% guidance) but management insists it is a logistics/timing slip (Middle-East vessel/container disruption stranded ~INR50 cr of finished goods; order book +18% YoY, ~INR906 cr executable in 12m), not lost share — so H1 FY27 execution is the key thing to verify.
